diagnosis: Failure class overcome: a SILENT OMITTED-ACTUATION no-op. The baseline (code.py, traces/) sampled a grasp pose for the red cube, moved the end-effector onto it, then executed lift -> place -> open_gripper without ever calling close_gripper(). Every primitive acted on an empty gripper. The keyframes are unambiguous: seed0_step003_goto_pose_after.png shows open fingers correctly straddling the red cube (perception, sample_grasp_pose and IK all healthy), seed0_step004_goto_pose_after.png shows the arm at the +0.2 post-pick height with the red cube still flat on the table, and seed0_step008_goto_pose_after.png shows both cubes still side-by-side at episode end. The winner (winner/program.py) inserts open_gripper() before the approach and close_gripper() after it, re-reads the green cube's pose after the pick has stepped physics, and adds a +0.005 release clearance. The winner's trace settles the single highest-risk unknown recorded in BLOCKED.md: close_gripper() RESOLVES and returns [ok] on all 3 debug seeds and all 5 validation seeds, so the feared NameError regression did not materialise. Scene settling is also confirmed as real and reproducible rather than a one-seed artifact: the green cube reads z=-0.087 at reset and z=-0.09710775 when re-read mid-episode, identically across all 8 episodes in both the baseline and winner traces. IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT ON THE WORD 'VALIDATED': the trace schema in this task contains only per-call fields (function, args, kwargs, status, result_summary, media, duration_ms, step). There is NO reward, success, solved or terminated field anywhere in winner/trace.json, winner/validation_trace.json or traces/trace.json, and winner/ carries no keyframe media. 'FAILURES: 0' is purely a count of non-ok primitive statuses, and the KNOWN-BROKEN baseline scores exactly the same FAILURES: 0 on that metric. No trace re-reads the red cube after release. Therefore the proposition 'the winner stacks the cubes' is NOT attested by any artifact in this directory; what IS attested is that the winner repairs a real, evidenced defect (the missing grasp) that made task success impossible, and that its added primitive resolves. The skills below are scoped to that evidence and deliberately exclude any claim of measured task success. A further concrete finding from validation seed 103: the green cube was displaced 3.35cm in y (-0.08668758 -> -0.05319031) and tumbled out of upright (quaternion moved from pure-yaw (0,0,0.773,-0.635) to (0.515,0.484,0.515,-0.484), a ~120deg rotation about a tilted axis) between the reset read and the pre-place read, i.e. the arm knocked the support cube while working on the neighbouring red cube. The winner's late re-read absorbed the position change, which is independent evidence for skill #2 beyond the settling rationale that originally motivated it.

proposed_skills.name: omitted-actuation-behind-an-all-ok-trace
proposed_skills.failure_signature: Every primitive returns [ok], the summary reports FAILURES: 0, yet the task is not accomplished and the target object's pose is unchanged between the first and last keyframe. Perception, grasp sampling and IK all look healthy in isolation, and no parameter looks wrong because no primitive complained.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any manipulation task whose trace shows no failed primitive but no object motion either: pick-and-place, stacking, insertion, put-in-container, drawer/door opening. Reach for this BEFORE re-tuning perception prompts, grasp poses or approach heights: a zero-failure trace actively misdirects toward those, because every primitive that did run really did work. The tell is that the failure is in an action that was never requested, not in one that errored.
proposed_skills.strategy: Stop triaging by status and triage by causal chain. Write down the primitives the task REQUIRES, then diff that list against the primitives the trace actually CONTAINS. A silent no-op episode is usually an omitted actuation primitive (close before transport, open before release, a missing lift) rather than a mis-parameterised one. Confirm by pairing the keyframe at the moment of the supposed state change against the object's pose: if the arm is at the lift height and the object is still on the table, the transport is carrying nothing. Before adding the missing call, verify the primitive's NAME against an evidenced source (an existing call in the program, the skill library, or a prior trace); guessing a name converts a silent no-op into a hard NameError and regresses below baseline. Here open_gripper() was attested in the baseline and close_gripper() was only inferred from its existence, which was correctly flagged as the top risk and then confirmed to resolve on replay.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# Trace shows:    sample_grasp_pose -> goto_pose(grasp) -> goto_pose(lift) -> open_gripper
# Task requires:  sample_grasp_pose -> goto_pose(grasp) -> CLOSE -> goto_pose(lift) -> open_gripper
#                                                          ^^^^^ absent from trace, never errored
pick_pos, pick_quat = sample_grasp_pose(obj)
open_gripper()                        # ensure fingers are open before the approach
goto_pose(pick_pos, pick_quat, z_approach=0.1)
close_gripper()                       # the omitted link in the causal chain
lift = pick_pos.copy(); lift[2] += 0.2
goto_pose(lift, pick_quat)

proposed_skills.name: assert-object-state-when-the-trace-has-no-reward-signal
proposed_skills.failure_signature: The harness reports a program as passing on the strength of 'FAILURES: 0' / all-ok statuses, but the trace schema contains no reward, success or solved field. A program that does nothing at all earns exactly the same score as one that solves the task, so the pass carries no information about the objective.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any task whose trace records only per-call status (function/args/status/result_summary/duration_ms) with no task-level outcome field. Check this BEFORE trusting a validation result or declaring a repair validated. It applies to every task type in such a harness, and is most urgent when the failure mode under repair is a silent no-op, because that is precisely the mode a status-only metric cannot see.
proposed_skills.strategy: Make the outcome observable from inside the program, using only permitted observation APIs. Re-read the MANIPULATED object's pose at the very end of the episode, compute the pose the task predicts, and record the comparison so the trace itself carries an outcome signal. This costs one extra call, needs no simulator access, and converts an unfalsifiable 'all primitives returned ok' into a checkable claim. Two corollaries: (a) do the same after the grasp (re-read the held object once the arm has lifted; if its z did not rise with the end-effector, the gripper closed on air), and (b) when reporting, keep 'the repair fixes a real defect' separate from 'the repair is measured to solve the task'; a status-only pass supports only the former.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# Status-only traces cannot distinguish 'did the task' from 'did nothing'.
# Re-read the moved object at the end so the trace records an outcome.
import numpy as np

# after place + open_gripper + retract:
held_final, _, _ = get_object_pose(held, return_bbox_extent=False)
support_final, _, _ = get_object_pose(support, return_bbox_extent=False)
expected_z = support_final[2] + support_ext[2]/2 + held_ext[2]/2
xy_err = float(np.linalg.norm(held_final[:2] - support_final[:2]))
z_err = float(abs(held_final[2] - expected_z))
# surfaces in result_summary / stdout -> becomes real evidence in the trace
print('STACK_CHECK ok=%s xy_err=%.4f z_err=%.4f' % (xy_err < 0.02 and z_err < 0.01, xy_err, z_err))

# Grasp check, same idea: if the held object did not rise with the arm, we grabbed air.
# held_after_lift, _, _ = get_object_pose(held, return_bbox_extent=False)
# print('GRASP_CHECK', held_after_lift[2] - held_rest_z > 0.05)

proposed_skills.name: relocalize-support-immediately-before-placement
proposed_skills.failure_signature: A pose read at reset disagrees with the same object's pose re-read later in the episode, with no intentional contact in between. Two distinct causes produce this: (a) settling, a consistent ~1cm z drop as spawned objects drop onto their support once physics steps (green cube z -0.087 -> -0.09710775 in every episode here), and (b) collateral disturbance, where the arm clips a neighbouring object while working (validation seed 103: support displaced 3.35cm in y and tumbled out of upright). Placements computed from the reset read land systematically high, or beside a support that is no longer there.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any task computing a placement, stacking or insertion target from a pose sampled before the arm has moved: stacking, put-on-shelf, put-in-container, insertion. Cheap enough to apply unconditionally. The disturbance case makes it valuable even in harnesses without spawn-settling, and it matters most when the manipulated and support objects start close together, where the approach is most likely to clip the support.
proposed_skills.strategy: Treat any pose read at t=0 as provisional. Re-read the SUPPORT object's position immediately before computing the placement target, after the pick has already stepped the sim; that single read absorbs both settling and any disturbance the arm caused on the way. Bounding-box extents are sizes, not poses, so they are unaffected by both and may safely be read once up front: refresh only the position. Add a small release clearance on top of the computed contact height so the held object is dropped a few millimetres rather than driven into its support. Two assumptions to keep in view: the sum-of-half-extents math is valid only because sample_grasp_pose returns the object's centre here, so the end-effector frame coincides with the held object's centre while grasped (verify this in a new harness rather than assuming it); and support_ext[2]/2 is the support's VERTICAL half-extent only while the support is upright, which seed 103 shows is not guaranteed. That approximation survived here only because a cube's extents are all equal; for a non-cube support, check the support's orientation before trusting it.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# Extents are stable -> read once. Positions settle and get knocked -> re-read late.
_, _, support_ext = get_object_pose(support, return_bbox_extent=True)
_, _, held_ext = get_object_pose(held, return_bbox_extent=True)

pick_pos, pick_quat = sample_grasp_pose(held)
open_gripper()
goto_pose(pick_pos, pick_quat, z_approach=0.1)
close_gripper()
lift = pick_pos.copy(); lift[2] += 0.2
goto_pose(lift, pick_quat)

# ... the pick above has stepped the sim, so read the support NOW, not at reset ...
support_pos, support_quat, _ = get_object_pose(support, return_bbox_extent=False)

# Guard the upright assumption behind the half-extent math (pure-yaw quat => upright).
# For a non-cube support, a tumbled support_quat invalidates support_ext[2] as 'height'.
place = support_pos.copy()
place[2] = support_pos[2] + support_ext[2]/2 + held_ext[2]/2 + 0.005  # release clearance
goto_pose(place, pick_quat, z_approach=0.1)
open_gripper()
